This guide goes from nothing to a poverty rate with its standard error. The code does not run when
the vignette is built, because it needs the INEI files.

## 1. What is there

```{r}
library(faperu)
fa_surveys()
fa_years("enaho")
fa_catalog("enaho", 2024)
```

Each source is one YAML file in `inst/catalog/`. Modules that were already downloaded once carry
their SHA-256, so faperu notices when INEI replaces a file.

## 2. Where files go

```{r}
fa_cache()                       # default user cache
fa_cache("~/data/inei")          # or a folder you choose
```

If you already have the zip files with the layout `<SURVEY>/<year>/<file>.zip`, point the cache
there and nothing will be downloaded again.

## 3. Download and read

```{r}
fa_download("enaho", 2024, "34")
s <- fa_read("enaho", 2024, "34", file = "Sumaria-2024\\.")
```

`fa_download()` returns one row per module with a `status`: `cached`, `downloaded` or `changed`.
`fa_read()` unzips next to the zip and reads the file you name; SPSS and Stata keep their labels.
The default format is Stata. To read only some variables, list them in `cols`; `fa_variables()`
shows the names and labels without reading the data:

```{r}
v <- fa_variables("enaho", 2024, "34", file = "Sumaria-2024\\.")
s8 <- fa_read("enaho", 2024, "34", file = "Sumaria-2024\\.",
              cols = c("conglome", "vivienda", "hogar", "ubigeo", "pobreza", "factor07", "mieperho"))
```

For a wide module this is much faster: 8 of the 1425 columns of the 2024 employment module take
about 0.6 s in Stata, against 10 s for the whole file.

## 4. Places, before the design

```{r}
s <- fa_ubigeo(s)
table(s$department_name)
```

Locate the data before weighting them: the territory decides which part of the sample you study,
and the design has to know it from the start.

District codes change: new provinces moved some districts to new codes, and new districts appear
every year. To compare years, translate the codes to one base year. The natural base is 2017, the
1874 districts of the 2017 Census, which every INEI survey since 2018 uses as its frame:

```{r}
s <- fa_ubigeo(s, year = 2024, base = 2017)
table(s$ubigeo_status)          # same, recoded, to_parent, multi_parent, ...
fa_districts(2017)              # the 1874 districts of the census frame
```

Codes are INEI's, always as six-digit text; RENIEC numbers districts differently from department 07
on. The equivalences come from INEI's municipal registry (RENAMU 2004-2025), its 2025 national
directory, the 2017 census frame and, for the 18 districts created after 2017, the 2017 district
that holds their schools in MINEDU's 2025 register, not yet checked law by law. Districts with two
parents (Lambras, Santa Lucia) and districts created between 2005 and 2017 get `NA`: faperu does
not guess. The sources and the method are in `system.file("ubigeo", "README.md", package =
"faperu")`.

## 5. Sampling design

```{r}
library(survey)
options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust")
d <- fa_design(s, "enaho")
svymean(~I(pobreza < 3), d)          # share of poor households: 0.219 (SE 0.004)

s$facpob <- s$factor07 * s$mieperho           # weight by persons, as INEI does
p <- fa_design(s, "enaho", weight = "facpob")
svymean(~I(pobreza < 3), p)                  # 0.276 (SE 0.005), INEI's official 27.6 % for 2024
svyby(~I(pobreza < 3), ~dominio, p, svymean)
```

The two numbers were computed with faperu 0.1.0 on the ENAHO 2024 files. The second one matches
the official monetary poverty rate published by INEI for 2024.

For the other surveys, as computed with faperu on the 2024 files:

```{r}
e <- read.csv("EPEN 2024 BD_Publicacion Dpto.csv", fileEncoding = "latin1")   # 935-Modulo76
d <- fa_design(e, "epen")                       # drops people under 14, who have no weight
svymean(~I(OCUP300 == 2), subset(d, OCUP300 %in% 1:2))     # unemployment 5.6 %
svymean(~I(Informal_P == 1), subset(d, OCUP300 == 1), na.rm = TRUE)  # informality 70.9 %

a <- fa_read("ena", 2024, "1911")               # chapter 1100
a <- a[a$p1102 %in% 1 & a$estrato != "", ]
svymean(~I(p1103 == 2), fa_design(a, "ena"), na.rm = TRUE)  # women producers 31.5 %
```

### One territory

To study one department, province or district, give it to `fa_design()` as `territory`. Do not
filter the rows first: that drops the strata and clusters of the rest of the country and the
standard errors come out wrong.

```{r}
puno <- fa_design(s, "enaho", weight = "facpob", territory = "Puno")   # or "21"
svymean(~I(pobreza < 3), puno)        # 0.399 (SE 0.0237), correct

# Wrong: filtering first gives the same estimate but SE 0.0230
# fa_design(s[substr(s$ubigeo, 1, 2) == "21", ], "enaho", weight = "facpob")
```

`territory` takes INEI codes of 2, 4 or 6 digits (`"21"`, `"2101"`, `"210101"`) or department
names, several at once. faperu builds the design on the whole sample and keeps only the territory
with `subset()`, which is how the survey package estimates a domain.

ENDES and the ENA have strata with a single cluster, so set
`options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust")` first; `fa_design()` warns when it is needed. ENUT and
ENARES publish no strata, and the Annual Economic Survey publishes none either: its firms included
with certainty go in their own stratum and the standard errors are approximate. See `?fa_design`.

`fa_design()` takes the weight, strata and cluster that the catalog declares. For ENAHO they are
`FACTOR07`, `ESTRATO` and `CONGLOME`; for ENDES, `V005` or `HV005` (divided by one million),
`V022` and `V001`. Any of them can be overridden, and a stratum can cross two columns: `strata = "CCDD*AREA"`.

### The ENA across rounds

The National Agricultural Survey changed several times between 2014 and 2025. What faperu does
for you, and what you have to keep in mind:

- **Stratum.** From 2023 the stratum is `ESTRATO`. From 2014 to 2022 `ESTRATO` is empty for
  producers (it only classifies the agricultural firms) or does not exist, and the stratum is
  `DOMINIO`. `fa_design()` picks the right one and warns (class `faperu_warning_ena_strata`) when
  it uses `DOMINIO`. Read `ESTRATO`, `DOMINIO` and `CODIGO` with your columns.
- **Two frames.** Agricultural firms (`CODIGO` 2) are a separate sampling frame. `fa_design()`
  keeps them in their own strata; from 2024 they are surveyed in full and add no variance. To
  study producers only, drop them before the design: removing a whole frame is safe.
- **Identifiers.** The cluster is `CONGLOMERADO` up to 2022 and `NSEGM` from 2023; the producer
  is `NSELUA` up to 2022 and `ID_PROD` from 2023. `fa_key(x, "ena")` builds the same key in every
  round, and joins the chapters of one round in full.
- **Not a panel.** The same key in two rounds is not the same farm: there are no common units
  between 2024 and 2025. Compare rounds by area with `fa_link()`, never unit by unit.
- **Questionnaire changes.** The livestock practices (`P501A_*`) had 22 items in 2014-2019, only
  6 (pastures) in 2021, and 30 with their years of adoption from 2022, when genetic improvement
  split into artificial insemination (`16C`), improved breeding stock (`16D`) and embryo
  transfer (`16E`). A series that includes 2021 must say so.
- **Labels.** The Stata labels of 2022-2025 are cut at 80 characters, so `16C` to `16E` look
  alike in `fa_variables()`. The full wording is in the data dictionary PDF inside each zip
  (`Diccionario_Datos_*.pdf`).
- **Data entry.** INEI's files keep some unit errors (in 2017 a few sales are a thousand times
  the production) and the 2019 production levels sit above the rest of the series. faperu does
  not change the data; check ratios such as sales over production before using them, and the
  reference period of 2019 in its technical sheet.

```{r}
ena <- fa_read("ena", 2017, "1315", file = "01_Cap100_1",
               cols = c("CONGLOMERADO", "ESTRATO", "DOMINIO", "FACTOR", "CODIGO"))
d <- fa_design(ena, "ena")    # DOMINIO as stratum, firms in their own strata
```

## 6. The 2017 Census

INEI does not publish the census microdata as a file. CELADE distributes the full database in
REDATAM format, and `fa_redatam()` queries it through the redatamx package (install it first; it is
only suggested). The first call downloads 678 MB into the cache.

```{r}
fa_redatam("freq PERSONA.C5P2")                     # 29 381 884 people, the official count
fa_redatam("freq DEPARTAM.CCDD by PERSONA.C5P2")
v <- fa_redatam()                                    # variables of every entity
```

## 7. New years

```{r}
fa_check_updates()
```

A row with `new = TRUE` is a year the source already publishes and the catalog does not have yet.

## Errors

Every error has class `faperu_error` and a subclass that says what went wrong:

```{r}
tryCatch(
  fa_download("enaho", 2024, "34"),
  faperu_error_download = function(e) message("INEI did not answer: ", conditionMessage(e))
)
```
